_comment: Measured values printed by the T.5.4 report figures. One entry per figure.
Each carries the decision-register entry that recorded it, so a figure can be
traced back without opening the plotting code. Editing a number here changes
the figure and nothing else; the scripts hold no numbers of their own.

placement_freedom_f2.source: docs/docs_decisions.md D86 (2026-09-02), scripts/f2_placement_freedom_check.py, configs/f2/check_{baseline,offsets}[_mw].yaml, 15 iterations/arm, all 4 arms clock_truncated_master_solves == 0
placement_freedom_f2.instance: Q = 2, T = 22, minute recourse, p_minutes = 56, policy = start, anticipate-only offset grid [-30,-15,0] (D76)
placement_freedom_f2.unit: lower bound, slot-equivalent units; gain is relative to the baseline arm's LB
placement_freedom_f2.verdict: Selection does not recover the F2 lever. Both LBs move up slightly under MW (marginally stronger cuts at each anchor, as expected), but the gap between the two arms -- what F2 is actually about -- is essentially unchanged and remains strongly negative under both cut generators. Report Sec 4.3.1's placement-freedom diagnosis is complete, not partial.

runtime_split.source: docs/docs_decisions.md D83 (2026-09-02), a standard Benders loop (configs/baseline_d9.yaml) with run.emit_reports=true, reading BendersRunResult / manifest['runtime'] (D71 instrumentation)
runtime_split.instance: baseline_d9.yaml, Q = 2, T = 22, p = 50 slot units (1500 pax-min regime), slot recourse, 10 iterations (this config's own fixed regression budget), single-threaded
runtime_split.note: supersedes nothing quotable -- the earlier 'master ~85.7% of runtime' figure was already withdrawn (PROJECT_STATE_v6 Sec 3, D71) and is not re-derived or refuted here; this is instrumentation exercised on a real run for the first time, not a like-for-like re-measurement of that withdrawn number.
runtime_split.cutadd_note: total_cutadd_time_s is tracked separately and is NOT one of the four terms the reconciliation above sums (it is small, 0.03% of wall time, and already inside model_management_overhead_s) -- matches the exact formula BendersRunResult's own tests assert (test_overhead_reconciles_the_split_to_the_wall_time).

distance_to_known_optimum_at_run_end.note: single end-of-run data point, not a time-to-threshold curve. B3's other half (time to within a fixed threshold of the optimum, over the run) is NOT implemented: no per-iteration timestamped incumbent trace exists in BendersRunResult or the manifest, only the final best_lower_bound/best_upper_bound. Restated, not newly discovered -- D71 already named this gap. Building that trace would be a code change out of this handout's scope.

start_zero_gain_cells.note: burst and spiky at delta=30 report exactly 0.00% gain -- flagged for investigation by the handout before recording (a de-aligned generator should not produce this by boundary alignment). Investigated (D81): the generator's alignment property is intact (0/150 burst arrivals and 5/150, 8/150 spiky arrivals land on exact multiples of 30, the latter consistent with flat's own 4/150 chance rate); a direct check confirmed the two monolithic MIPs (slot recourse, minute recourse), independently formulated and solved, chose the BIT-IDENTICAL first-stage schedule (same departure slots for both vehicles, both directions) at delta=30 for these two shapes only, at every finer delta (15, 10) the schedules differ and the gain is positive. Reading: at the coarsest resolution the first-stage combinatorial choice is constrained enough (T=22 slots, Q=2) that the two objectives -- slot-aggregate wait vs exact-minute wait -- happen to rank the same schedule best for burst/spiky's own demand pattern; at finer resolutions there is more scheduling freedom and the two objectives diverge. Not a generator regression.
